title: The Lost Bell
skill_description: Practice reading words with final consonant blends (-nd, -mp, -st, -nt, -ll) and doubled consonants (ff, ll, ss).
author: FunBookies
summary: Ben finds an old bell at a castle ruin. He rings it and goes back in time — the castle is alive with banners and people. He sees men on the wall, a big gate slamming shut, and a woman at the well. Then the bell rings again and he is back in the quiet ruin.
visual_style: Rich watercolor with warm stone textures and golden light. The past is vivid and bustling — bright banners, warm sun, busy people. The present is quiet, mossy, overgrown. The contrast tells the story.

pages.text: Ben finds an old bell at a castle ruin. When he rings it, the castle comes back to life — guards, banners, and all. What will he see before the bell rings again?

reference_prompt:
9-panel children's book reference sheet, rich watercolor style with warm stone textures and golden light.

Row 1 - CHARACTER:
[1] Ben front view: small boy (5-6), short messy brown hair, round face, red tunic shirt, brown shorts, brown lace-up boots, curious bright expression. Standing pose holding a tarnished bronze bell.
[2] Ben action: running up stone steps, hair bouncing, boots on worn stone, one hand on wall. Dynamic upward movement.
[3] Ben windswept: standing on castle battlements, wind blowing hair and shirt sideways, one hand gripping stone parapet, looking out at vast green landscape.

Row 2 - KEY ELEMENTS:
[4] The bronze bell: tarnished green-brown patina, classic bell shape, clapper visible inside. Golden light radiating from it in all directions.
[5] **HERO SHOT**: The castle alive — tall clean stone walls with bright red and gold banners, clear blue moat, drawbridge down, warm golden sunlight, blue sky. Vivid and bustling.
[6] The castle in ruin — same structure but crumbling, thick moss and ivy covering the walls, empty dark windows, stagnant green moat. Grey-green muted tones. Silent.

Row 3 - SETTINGS:
[7] Castle wall battlements from below: crenellated walkway at top of tall stone walls, three soldiers silhouetted against sky, colourful banners fluttering. Warm golden light.
[8] Stone well in courtyard: circular low stone wall, wooden crossbar with rope and bucket, cobblestones around it, a medieval woman in linen dress and headscarf. Warm busy sunlit scene.
[9] Massive wooden castle gate: heavy timber with iron studs, closed in a thick stone archway, two guards with spears standing beside it. Warm torchlight on stone.

Palette: warm stone grey-brown, moss green, sunset gold, bronze bell patina, Ben's red shirt and brown hair. Past scenes = warm golden. Present scenes = cool grey-green.
Format: Square 1:1, 3x3 grid, thin white borders between panels.
CRITICAL: NO TEXT, NO WORDS, NO LETTERS anywhere in the image.

parent_tips.before_reading: Look at the cover together. Ask: What do you see? Why does the castle look two different ways? What do you think the bell does?
parent_tips.during_reading: When the castle changes, ask: What is different now? Point out the castle features — the wall for watching, the gate for keeping people out, the well for water. Ask: Why did castles need these things?
parent_tips.after_reading: Talk about what Ben saw in the past. Why did castles have walls so tall? What was the well for? What would it be like to live in a castle? Would you ring the bell again?

comprehension_questions.question: What did Ben find at the castle?
comprehension_questions.answer: An old bell in the sand.

comprehension_questions.question: What happened when he rang the bell?
comprehension_questions.answer: The castle came back to life — it was strong and tall again with people in it.

comprehension_questions.question: What did the men on the wall do?
comprehension_questions.answer: They watched the land from up on top to see who was coming.

comprehension_questions.question: What was the well for?
comprehension_questions.answer: It held all the water for the castle.

comprehension_questions.question: What happened at the end?
comprehension_questions.answer: The bell rang again and the castle went back to a ruin, but Ben kept the bell.
